system.summary: Homophonic letter substitution with single signs for names, only sensitive words enciphered.
system.notes: No Norreys key on DECODE; the Cecil-Norris 1568 table reconstructed by Tomokiyo from Cabala (1663) fits. Signs may be turned in any orientation; single signs for persons.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's partial Cecil-Norris key (cryptiana, from Cabala 1663); CSP Foreign viii summaries. No published decipherment of these Norreys passages found.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: Tomokiyo Cecil-Norris table applied by hand

solution.what: Fetched R9251, R9250 and key records R9257, R9260-R9262 images from DECODE.
Compared the Throckmorton first, second and third alphabets and the Smith key with Norreys's signs.
Tokenised all seven Norreys extracts (transcription.txt); the date is 9 Mar 1567/8 = 1568.
Located the seven letters in CSP Foreign viii (BHO) as cribs.
Name signs Xr, Ec, fk recur in 9 Feb and 24 Feb in the calendar's order Protestants / Prince / Admiral; Lesley and Scotland fit 6 Feb groups 1 and 4.
Aligned 'the Protestants' and 'and England' in the 4 June passage; conflicts with the 6 Feb alignment (s: = e vs a).
Backtracking assignment of groups to calendar vocabulary under a consistent sign map.
Found Tomokiyo's Cecil-Norris cipher table (from the Cabala 'Postscript' of 27 Sept 1568) on cryptiana elizabeth.htm.
Applied it: 9 Feb demaund, reason, ruin; 24 Feb remain; 6 July 1567 Master Stewarde; all match CSP summaries.
Target 9 Mar 1568: (1) French King name sign (H), (2) 'Catholic' abbreviated (M), (3) name sign, Queen of Scots? (I).

Tomokiyo table applied by script to every tokenised group (work/tomokiyo_apply.py): adds 10 July 1567 'the lord of Murrei', 4 June 1567 'Savoia ... intend to ouerthrou ... and England', 6 Feb 1568 Leisly, Earl, Rothes, papystes, reaums, stayid; 9 Feb reason, ruin; 24 Feb remayn. Corrects 6 Feb (4) to 'papystes' (not Scotland).
Same tokens with the table's letter values shuffled among signs, 1000 seeded trials, scored by dictionary-word hits: real 8, shuffled mean 0.22, max 3; no shuffle yields a cribbed word.

Target 9 Mar 1568 re-examined on the image: (2) is four signs, tentatively 'Pope' (grade I), revising the first pass's 'Catholic' (M); (1) and (3) are nomenclator name signs, not in the table, left unread (first pass's French King identification withdrawn as too loose).

Target 9 Mar 1568 settled: (1) French King name sign restored (H, same sign as 6 Feb 5/13, 9 Feb 5); (2) 'a t ? l' not read, 'Pope' and 'Catholic' rejected on Cabala p.152 (crossed arrowhead is not p); (3) Queen of Scots? by position (I).

outcome.method_basis: The key is Tomokiyo's published reconstruction of the Cecil-Norris cipher of 1567-70 (cryptiana elizabeth.htm, from the Cabala 1663 'Postscript'), found during the attempt after crib searches against CSP Foreign viii failed, and applied to the Norreys extracts in Forbes's file (Add MS 4136).
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: cipher signs of the 9 Mar 1568 target, 2 of 6 read (item 1 name sign H, item 3 name sign I; the four signs of item 2 unread). Siblings (work/tomokiyo_apply.out): 38 of 51 groups read, the 13 garbled groups listed in gaps counted unread.
outcome.notes: Sibling readings verified against CSP Foreign viii summaries and a shuffle control; target item 1 French King (H), item 2 not read, item 3 Queen of Scots? (I). fraction_read 0.33 is measured on the target 9 Mar 1568 extract only (2 of 6 signs).
